It is painfully obvious that this artificial difficulty and matchmaking manipulation are designed strictly to stall your rank progression, frustrate you, and trap you in an endless loop of engagement.
To make matters worse, the player acquisition system is downright predatory. The odds on epic player spins are abysmal, with the game almost always holding out until the very last possible pulls to drain every last coin you’ve saved or paid for. I think the Smart Assist option should have two additional sub-options to give players more control and improve the overall gameplay experience:
1. Smart Power Shooting - Automatically adjusts the shooting power based on the player's position, distance from the goal, and situation.
2. Smart Auto Clear (Defensive Line) - Automatically clears the ball when a defender is under heavy pressure or when clearing the ball is the safest option.
However, these features should be separately selectable. For example, I may want to use Smart Power Shooting without using Smart Auto Clear. I should be able to turn each option on or off independently according to my preference.

This is not just my personal preference—- many players would like to have this kind of flexibility as well. Giving players the ability to choose which smart assist feature they want to use would make the system much more flexible, user-friendly, and suitable for different play styles

author: Abdull:2029
title: From the Middle East
content:
To KONAMI and the eFootball Development Team,

We are writing this as a community that has supported eFootball for years, invested our time and money into the game, and continued to stand by it despite countless frustrations.

But we have reached a point where remaining silent is no longer acceptable.

The current state of eFootball is deeply disappointing.

The impact of what players commonly describe as “the script” has become increasingly difficult to ignore. Matches often feel inconsistent and unpredictable, with player responsiveness, passing, movement, rebounds, and finishing appearing to change dramatically from one moment to another.

A competitive football game should reward skill, decision-making, timing, and consistency.

It should NOT leave players feeling that the outcome of a match is being influenced by factors outside their control.

However, the scripting issue is only one part of a much larger problem.

THE CONNECTION QUALITY IS UNACCEPTABLE

Players across North Africa and the Middle East continue to suffer from unstable connections, high latency, input delay, and inconsistent gameplay.

And the most important question remains:

Where are the dedicated servers for our region?

North Africa and the Middle East contain a massive and highly active eFootball player base. Yet players in these regions are still expected to compete under conditions that can put them at a significant disadvantage compared with players located closer to major server infrastructure.

This is not simply a minor inconvenience.

In a competitive online football game, connection quality directly affects gameplay and competitive fairness.

When a player's commands are delayed, when players feel unresponsive, when passes take longer to execute, and when matches become dependent on connection quality rather than football ability, the competitive experience is fundamentally damaged.

WE ARE NOT ASKING FOR SPECIAL TREATMENT.

We are asking for FAIR TREATMENT.

We are asking KONAMI to recognize the North African and Middle Eastern communities as an important part of the global eFootball ecosystem.

We want:

• Dedicated and properly optimized server infrastructure for North Africa and the Middle East.

• Significant improvements to matchmaking and connection stability.

• Greater transparency regarding server locations and matchmaking systems.

• A serious investigation into the gameplay inconsistencies that players experience and commonly describe as “scripting.”

• Clear communication with the community regarding these issues and the steps being taken to address them.

• A competitive environment where skill, not connection quality or unexplained gameplay behavior, determines the result.

We have supported this game.

We have promoted it.

We have created content around it.

We have spent countless hours playing it.

Many of us have also spent real money supporting the game.

The least we deserve is to be heard.

This is not an attack on KONAMI.

This is a demand for accountability, transparency, and improvement.

We are not calling for insults, harassment, or disrespect toward KONAMI or its employees.

Instead, we are calling for something far more powerful:

A UNITED COMMUNITY DEMANDING A BETTER GAME.

If our concerns continue to be ignored, we will organize a peaceful and respectful community campaign to make these issues impossible to overlook.

Our message is simple:

We love football.
We love competition.
We love eFootball.
But we will not accept an unfair competitive experience indefinitely.

KONAMI, listen to your players.

North Africa is here.
The Middle East is here.
And we are asking you to finally treat our region as a serious part of the eFootball community.

We want answers.
We want action.
And most importantly, we want FAIR PLAY.

#eFootball
#FixTheServers
#MiddleEastServers
#NorthAfricaServers
#FairPlay
#FixeFootball

author: MOHAMED ELKHAYATE
title: eFootball Review
content:
The gameplay is extremely frustrating and often feels unfair.

The amount of glitches during matches is unacceptable. Players randomly freeze, fail to react to simple situations, make completely unnecessary movements, and sometimes ignore basic commands. These issues can directly decide the outcome of a match.

The balance of physical strength is also completely broken. Stronger players can easily lose physical battles against weaker players, while players with better speed, strength, or defensive stats often behave like they have no advantage at all. The stats on the card frequently don’t match what actually happens on the pitch.

The game also suffers from inconsistent player reactions, terrible collision detection, random rebounds, delayed inputs, and ridiculous animations. You can make the correct decision and execute the correct command, yet the game decides to do something completely different.

At this point, too many matches feel like they are being decided by glitches, random animations, and broken mechanics rather than actual gameplay.

The current gameplay needs serious fixing.

author: chan mya sahn
title: VAR can make more realistic game
content:
I think adding a VAR (Video Assistant Referee) system to eFootball would make the game more realistic and immersive, and many players would probably enjoy it.

VAR could be used for important or controversial situations such as goals, penalties, red cards, and offsides. For example, the referee might initially award a goal, then VAR checks the replay, detects an offside, and the screen shows “GOAL DISALLOWED – OFFSIDE.”

The main issue would be maintaining the flow of the game. VAR reviews should therefore be short—perhaps 5–10 seconds—and limited to genuinely close decisions, with an option to skip the review animation.

If implemented properly, VAR could add tension, uncertainty, and realism, making eFootball feel closer to watching and playing a real football match.

content:
سلام عليكم 

نحن مجموعة من لاعبي eFootball، نرغب في إيصال بعض الملاحظات والاقتراحات إلى فريق KONAMI، ونتمنى أخذها بعين الاعتبار في التحديثات القادمة.
